recap.text: Limp Richard is a short, squat Mole Man shopkeeper at transfer station 83 who reads physical books. Crawler Donut negotiates a padded mallet down to 150 gold. Carl trades five westerns for five of Richard's books, then trades his remaining westerns and a jug of moonshine for a dwarven Battery Fabricator and fifty batteries. The fabricator turns mana potions and metal blocks into batteries.

beats.headline: Supplies for the weary
beats.text: For the record: at the top of the stairs at transfer station 83 stand a saferoom, a mace and bashing weapons guild, and Limp Richard's Sundries. Subject is a Mole Man, level thirty-six, non-combatant, short and squat, glasses, reading a book in his open doorway. The system's note on his kind: they call themselves Men and Women, which is exhausting, and spend their days and nights reading. Welcome to station 83, says subject. Supplies for the weary travellers. Crawler Carl says they are weary, and they'll be by after they sleep. Suit yourself.
beats.gist: Limp Richard, a short, squat Mole Man with glasses, sells sundries at transfer station 83.

beats.headline: Price not negotiable
beats.text: Subject's stock is wide and mostly useless. Crawler Donut talks a padded mallet down from 250 gold to 150 and then negotiates all the patience out of him on a pile of junk. In a dusty corner sits a Battery Fabricator, 75,000 gold, lifted from a dwarven automaton factory: pour in mana potions, insert a metal block, a charged battery comes out. Box of fifty. Price not negotiable. How much charge? Ask a dwarf, says subject. Better than elven soul gems, which run on actual souls.
beats.gist: Donut buys a padded mallet for 150 gold from Limp Richard and buys junk.

beats.headline: Fifteen books, read to pieces
beats.text: Subject is reading an Andre Norton, and says a lot of his books are about cats. Crawler Carl says Norton was a woman. Shopkeepers get no entertainment feeds, subject explains, only physical media, and he has fifteen books, sixteen counting the one with the last chapters torn out. He has read this one dozens of times. Carl trades five westerns he has already read for five of his; subject has never read a western and notes they are short. Don't give the rest to the other mole men. Book hogs.
beats.gist: Limp Richard trades five books for five westerns with Carl.

beats.headline: Westerns for a fabricator
beats.text: A trade entered after the fact, as Crawler Carl files it: he traded the rest of his westerns and a single jug of moonshine for the dwarven Battery Fabricator, and the moleman shopkeeper practically begged him to, having finished the first five. Carl suspected the machine's odd placement in the first store he came across was no coincidence. It came with fifty batteries, five fully charged and five at half, and they are the same dwarven batteries the trainyard's repair carts run on.
beats.gist: Carl trades his remaining westerns and one jug of moonshine for a dwarven Battery Fabricator.
